title: Abstract the hypothesis to a predicate, prove its API, then instantiate (IMO 2024 P2)
intent: Hide the problem's existential hypothesis behind a predicate `Condition a b` and prove every fact about `(a, b)` as a lemma over an arbitrary witness `h : Condition a b`; only at the very end is the concrete witness built and the generalised lemmas instantiated, so no proof ever unfolds `Condition`.

parent.name: imo2024_p2
parent.statement:
problem imo2024_p2 (a b : ℕ+) :
    (a, b) ∈ solutionSet ↔
    ∃ g N : ℕ+,
      ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → Nat.gcd (a^n + b) (b^n + a) = g

children.name: condition_api (generalise)
children.statement:
variable {a b : ℕ} (h : Condition a b)

lemma gcd_eq_g {n : ℕ} (hn : h.N ≤ n) : Nat.gcd (a ^ n + b) (b ^ n + a) = h.g := h.N_spec.2.2 n hn
children.closed_by: each API lemma projects from the witness and rewrites: `a_pos : 0 < a := h.1`; `b_pos : 0 < b := h.2.1`; `g : ℕ := h.2.2.choose`; `g_spec := h.2.2.choose_spec`; `N : ℕ := h.g_spec.choose`; `N_spec := h.g_spec.choose_spec`; `g_pos := h.N_spec.1`; `N_pos := h.N_spec.2.1`; `gcd_eq_g := h.N_spec.2.2 n hn`; `symm` by `refine ⟨h.b_pos, h.a_pos, h.g, h.N, h.g_pos, h.N_pos, fun n hn ↦ ?_⟩` then `rw [Nat.gcd_comm]`; `dvd_g_of_le_N_of_dvd` by `rw [← h.gcd_eq_g hn, Nat.dvd_gcd_iff]`. The definition of `Condition` is never unfolded.

children.name: instantiation (hc : Condition a b)
children.statement: (a, b) ∈ solutionSet — the ← direction of imo2024_p2 (line 206)
children.closed_by: `have hc : Condition a b := by refine ⟨ha, hb, ?_⟩; obtain ⟨g, N, HCm⟩ := h; use g, N; refine ⟨g.pos, N.pos, ?_⟩; exact fun n a ↦ HCm n a` (lines 209-214); then the two generalised lemmas `PNat.coe_eq_one_iff.mp (hc.a_eq_one)` and `PNat.coe_eq_one_iff.mp (hc.b_eq_one)` (lines 216-217).

applicability.goal_shape: A goal whose hypothesis is an existential or other packaged condition that is used repeatedly by many lemmas with different conclusions. The move factors it into a predicate and proves all downstream facts over an arbitrary witness of that predicate, then reconstructs the concrete witness once at the end.
applicability.use_when: the same hypothesis is needed by several lemmas; the concrete witness would clutter each statement; the needed facts can be stated as accessor lemmas (here `h.1`, `h.2.1`, `h.2.2.choose_spec`) so the predicate is never unfolded again.
applicability.avoid_when: the witness must be chosen or transformed inside a proof in a way the accessors cannot express; the predicate is used only once (indirection is not worth it); or a proof genuinely needs to unfold the definition, in which case a different decomposition fits better.

claims.claim: The author names the abstraction and its derived quantities, signalling an interface meant to be used rather than unfolded: `Condition` is documented as 'The condition of the problem.' (line 43) and `g` as 'The value of `g` in the problem (determined by `a` and `b`).' (line 66).

The generalised API is instantiated a second time inside the development itself: `symm : Condition b a` (lines 84-87) constructs a swapped witness, and the b-side results are obtained by instantiating the a-side ones — `b_eq_one := h.symm.a_eq_one` (line 189) and `ab_add_one_dvd_b_pow_large_n_add_a` via `convert h.symm.ab_add_one_dvd_a_pow_large_n_add_b` (lines 154-157).

consequences: The move turns one existential hypothesis into a predicate plus a fixed set of accessor lemmas, so every later fact about the hypothesis must go through those accessors rather than re-deriving from the existential; adding a fact means first adding (and proving) another API lemma. `noncomputable def g`/`N` via `choose` make the API only partially computational, so each property needs `choose_spec`; that is fine here because nothing unfolds the predicate. The indirection concentrates all dependence on the concrete witness in one place (lines 209-214): the parent's sufficiency rests on `hc` satisfying exactly the same interface, and a client that later needs a stronger witness must generalise the predicate again.
